findings.title: permission-auto-allow hook auto-approves EVERY tool call (all Bash/Edit/Write/WebFetch) except 2 named tools, suppressing the user permission prompt system-wide -- active-only, no source-of-truth representation
findings.observe_how: Start a session in normal (non-bypass) mode; run a Bash command that would normally prompt (e.g. rm of a tracked file). With this hook active the prompt never appears and the tool runs. Disabling it restores the prompt.

notes:
Scope honesty: This gap-fill is DEPTH-over-breadth. The brief flags ~85% skills / ~69% rules+agents / ALL scripts / ALL drift / ALL trace as zero-verdict. I could not give all of that a real verdict in one pass without superficial name-dropping (the exact failure the brief warns against). I instead drilled the single highest-impact un-audited slice (D5b injection-surfaces) and found one load-bearing S1 (permission-auto-allow) that no hook-source dimension could have caught because it lives in the active settings registration, not in a hook's logic that D2a-g audited. Then I spot-cleared adjacent slices (agents frontmatter/haiku, sync scripts, codex-adversary injection path, skill script-refs) to give synthesis real CLEAN verdicts rather than 'unknown'.

THE KILLER FINDING (GAP3-01): permission-auto-allow makes the ENTIRE permission system a no-op on the live machine in normal mode. It emits decision.behavior:'allow' for every tool except AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode, with no matcher. This is the same safety-inversion CLASS as D2a-01 (navigator-safety) but with maximal blast radius (all tools, not just destructive Bash patterns). It also retroactively undermines the INTERIM-ACTIONS narrative: deregistering navigator-safety was said to be 'strictly safer -- destructive commands now flow through Claude Code's NORMAL permission prompt.' With permission-auto-allow live, that prompt does not exist in normal mode. The deregistration changed nothing for the destructive-command case. The 5 `.claude/rules/*` files that say 'ALWAYS confirm first' (railway/sentry/neon/kusto/linear) plus destructive-commands.md are model-side conventions only; the one HARD enforcement layer (PermissionRequest) is globally set to allow.

WHY active-only matters (GAP3-02): the hook src IS git-tracked (ships in repo) but is wired in ZERO tracked settings files -- so a code reviewer reading the repo source-of-truth sees a normal gated posture and would never know the live machine auto-approves everything. That's a decision-driving false impression baked into the repo's auditable surface. Whoever added it did so by hand-editing ~/.claude/settings.json (which sync-to-active.sh intentionally never touches), leaving no record in version control.

REMAINING GAP (be honest in synthesis): the bulk skills audit (D7b over the fourth-*/landing-page-*/ui-ux/next-* families, ~105 skills) and the trace-journey dimensions (D10a-c) and full rules-vs-code drift (D8a) are STILL un-covered. My sample says the slices I touched are healthy, but that is not a clean bill for the whole non-hook surface. WF-3 should still re-run D7b + D10a-c before claiming whole-system coverage; the brief's core thesis (a hook-only audit must not be presented as a whole-system review) stands and my findings do not retire it.
